title: timing/visual_events/actN.json
description: The beats an act's picture lands, exported for sound and QA (the films' v2 beat vocabulary). An act with no beats says so: {"silent": true, "reason": "…"}. The films named their character kind after the character; here it is "character". Time: t is always the beat, the film second the motion lands (its contact). A sustained motion also carries its span, start (film seconds) and dur (seconds): a draw and a count end on t (t = start + dur), a whoosh and a swell peak on t, inside the span. A draw and a count must give their span; any other kind may. The films timed one act's sustained draw at its start and said elsewhere that a draw ends on t, so the sound engine had to guess; the explicit span removes the guess. slate.timing.beats.problems() checks what a schema can't: t sits inside its span, and a draw or a count ends on t.

t.description: the beat: the film second the motion lands (a draw's or a count's end, a whoosh's or a swell's peak)

start.description: film seconds where a sustained motion begins

dur.description: seconds the sustained motion runs, from start

to.description: a count's last value, reached at t

x.description: where across the frame it happens, in pixels (for pan)

source.description: where the beat came from when it isn't the act's own code, e.g. capture:<name>

word.description: the voice's word the beat lands on (with occ for a repeat and offset in seconds): the sync gate holds it within two frames of the word, or for a character beat on or before its stressed syllable ends

occ.description: which time the word is said (1 is the first)

offset.description: seconds after the word's start the beat is meant to land

sync_exception.description: why the beat lands off its word on purpose: a REVIEW item for a person, never a silent pass

gesture.description: a character beat's gesture (turn, pulse, wave …), from the kit's motifBeats

stress_start.description: a character beat keyed to a word: film seconds its stressed syllable starts (the kit's contact is that frame plus 2)

stress_end.description: a character beat keyed to a word: film seconds its stressed syllable ends; the gesture lands on or before it
